Would like to keep dts examples in the dts places.  EM doesn't interact with dts directly, so having documentation here isn't the right place.  Push to the linux kernel, and just provide a link back to the device tree here.
Acknowledged
How about dropping all of this repeated stuff that isn't relevant for the mux and just distill it down to mux related topics?
Acknowledged

Overall, there's a ton of overlap in this doc with other docs, and not enough pointers to "Here's the platform that does this".  I'm all for getting the documentation better, but please lets keep what we have organized.
Acknowledged

Please label this as bmc.

And label the connector.
Acknowledged
Just call this a "card" or whatever device it is.  "Profile" implies that these are reused.
Acknowledged

Documentation of dts should really be going to dts in the linux kernel.  EM isn't even a user of the device tree;  You could probably just point to an upstream example here if you want some example of an i2c switch.
Acknowledged
You've called this a "card" but you haven't laid out which parts go in the baseboard config, and which parts go in the EM config.  Please make sure you have two files for this.
Acknowledged
Remove.  This is fluff;  If folks are reading this doc, they've already decided to use EM.
Acknowledged
nit, can you remove the majority of the "we" from this doc?  In 3 sentences all 3 start with "we".  This doc should focus on what's being done, and what it's being done to.
Acknowledged
Best practice is not to name based on $bus.  Some companies choose that, but in general we should be picking names that are useful to the user.
Acknowledged
